title: All Valid Triplets That Can Represent a Country
statement:
Three schools each list their students in a table of the same shape:

- `SchoolA(student_id, student_name)`, `SchoolB(student_id, student_name)` and `SchoolC(student_id, student_name)`: one row per student of that school; `student_id` is unique within each table, but the same id or name may appear in more than one school.

A country is represented by a team of three: one student from `SchoolA`, one from `SchoolB` and one from `SchoolC`. A team is valid only when its three members have three **different** `student_id` values and three **different** `student_name` values. List every valid team with the columns `member_A`, `member_B` and `member_C`, holding the names of the members chosen from `SchoolA`, `SchoolB` and `SchoolC`. Rows may come in any order.
constraints: student_id is unique within each of SchoolA, SchoolB and SchoolC
Names compare without regard to case, as in MySQL
reference:
SELECT a.student_name AS member_A,
  b.student_name AS member_B,
  c.student_name AS member_C
FROM SchoolA AS a
JOIN SchoolB AS b
  ON b.student_id <> a.student_id
  AND b.student_name <> a.student_name
JOIN SchoolC AS c
  ON c.student_id NOT IN (a.student_id, b.student_id)
  AND c.student_name NOT IN (a.student_name, b.student_name);
brute:
SELECT a.student_name AS member_A, b.student_name AS member_B, c.student_name AS member_C
FROM SchoolA AS a
CROSS JOIN SchoolB AS b
CROSS JOIN SchoolC AS c
WHERE NOT (a.student_id = b.student_id OR a.student_id = c.student_id OR b.student_id = c.student_id)
  AND NOT (a.student_name = b.student_name OR a.student_name = c.student_name OR b.student_name = c.student_name)
notes:
## Intuition

A team is one row from each school, so the candidate teams are all combinations of the three tables. Rather than building every combination and filtering afterwards, each **join condition** can reject clashes as soon as a new member is added: B must differ from A, and C must differ from both A and B, in id and in name.

## Approach

1. Start from `SchoolA` (alias `a`).
2. `JOIN SchoolB` (alias `b`) on `b.student_id <> a.student_id` and `b.student_name <> a.student_name`, keeping only pairs that do not clash.
3. `JOIN SchoolC` (alias `c`) on `c.student_id NOT IN (a.student_id, b.student_id)` and `c.student_name NOT IN (a.student_name, b.student_name)`.
4. Select the three names as `member_A`, `member_B` and `member_C`.

## Example 1, step by step

- A–B pairs: (Alice 1, Tom 3) and (Bob 2, Tom 3); both have different ids and names.
- For (Alice, Tom): Tom 3 from C repeats id 3 and the name Tom; Alice 10 repeats the name Alice; Jerry 2 is fine. Team: Alice, Tom, Jerry.
- For (Bob, Tom): Tom 3 clashes again; Jerry 2 shares id 2 with Bob; Alice 10 is fine. Team: Bob, Tom, Alice.

## Complexity

- Time: O(A · B · C) in the worst case, since every combination may be valid and must be output.
- Space: O(A · B · C) for the result in that worst case.

## Pitfalls

- Checking only the neighbouring pairs (A with B, B with C) misses a clash between A and C; all three pairs must differ.
- Both rules matter: different ids **and** different names. Dropping either one admits teams such as Bob 2 with Jerry 2.
- Writing the C conditions as `c.student_id <> a.student_id OR c.student_id <> b.student_id` is still true when C clashes with only one of them, so the clash slips through; each pair needs its own `AND`.

## Clauses

| Name | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `a` | the member from `SchoolA` |
| `b` | the member from `SchoolB`, already different from `a` |
| `c` | the member from `SchoolC`, different from both `a` and `b` |
| `member_A`, `member_B`, `member_C` | the three chosen names |

narration.1: The output columns are the names of the three chosen members, one per school.
narration.4: Every student of SchoolA starts a possible team.
narration.5: Pair each A student with SchoolB students, but only those that do not clash.
narration.6: The SchoolB member must have a different id from the SchoolA member ...
narration.7: ... and a different name, so the pair is already valid.
narration.8: Add a SchoolC student to every surviving pair.
narration.9: Their id must differ from both earlier members.
narration.10: Their name must also differ from both, which completes a valid team.
